neighbours.label: broadcast-medium words naming how media is delivered (' radio', ' TV', ' online') in station/channel contexts
fire: Most people in the valley still get their news from local radio stations.
The concert will be carried live on national radio tomorrow night.
After the storm, residents tuned their radio sets to the emergency channel.
Her talk show moved from radio to TV after its third season.
Fans can stream every match online or follow it on community radio.
The election debate aired on public TV and was replayed on radio.
In the 1950s the family gathered around the radio every evening.
The league sold rights to the games to three regional radio networks.
quiet: Most people in the valley still get their news from the weekly newspaper.
The concert will be held in the town square tomorrow night.
After the storm, residents gathered at the church to hear announcements.
Her advice column moved from the magazine to a book after its third year.
Fans can buy tickets at the gate or follow the match in the paper.
The election debate took place in the town hall and drew a big crowd.
In the 1950s the family gathered around the table every evening.
The league sold rights to the games to three regional newspapers.
